title: The Boy from the Poldi Chimneys

paragraphs.text: I was born in Kladno in 1946. From our window we looked straight at the chimneys of the Poldi steelworks, and my dad Frank worked at the furnace there, on shifts, nights too.
My mum Anna baked the best buns in all of Kladno, with poppy seeds and with plum jam. Every Saturday the whole house smelled of them.
My little sister Vera was four years younger, always hanging on to my trousers. We both waited by the oven to see who would get the first bun.
I spent most of my time with Pepa Walker, who lived in the house next door and was two years younger than me. We played football on the patch behind our building until dark.

openQuestions: How did running off to the fair in Prague with Pepa end?
Which school did you go to in Kladno?
